title: Make the price import stop at the first bad line

blocks.text: Every night a supplier sends a price file, one `SKU;cents` line per product, with `#` comments and blank lines in between. Last week a file arrived with a broken line in the middle. The import should have stopped there so that someone could fix the file and run it again, but half a file of prices went live, and nobody was told which line was wrong.

`PriceImport` already parses a line (`parse` throws the checked `BadLineException`), recognises comments and stores a price. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/PriceImport.java`: `importAll(lines)`, which returns how many prices it stored.

When you're done, a good file is stored in full, and the first bad line ends the import: the prices before it stay, nothing after it is stored, and the caller's `catch (PriceImport.BadLineException e)` gets the line's number as an editor would show it. About eight lines.

cases.says: every price of a file with no bad line is stored, in file order, and counted
comment lines and blank lines are skipped and not counted
a bad line ends the import: the prices before it stay stored and none after it is stored
the caller gets the checked BadLineException for the first bad line
the bad line's number counts every line of the file, comments and blank lines included

origin.section: A Loop Is Clearer When the Work Stops Early, Throws a Checked Exception, or Updates Several Variables

concepts: A loop is clearer than a stream when the work must stop early, throw a checked exception or track positions and several totals; return in a forEach lambda only skips one element.
